answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie reputation to staked work history rather than identity alone. Each agent earns standing slowly, like a tide building over time, and loses it fast if it misbehaves. Newcomers start with a violet-tinted probationary badge that limits high-value actions until they prove reliability, so flooding the network with fresh clones buys nothing. A walnut-shell test helps too: random spot-checks ask agents to prove past work, and shells with no kernel inside get discarded. Sybils stay expensive and useless.
